items.explanation_consistent: 해설이 정답·오답 판단과 일치하고 글자 참조가 맞으면 true

items.passage: I had been Gopal's apprentice in the bookbinding workshop in Dhaka for only a year when we were hired to empty a widow's house. My name is Efua, and I was restless then; I wanted to sort everything into piles and be done by noon. Gopal moved slowly, opening each ledger and letter as if it might speak. By evening only one item remained: a ragged prayer book with its spine split in three places. I offered to throw it on the cart. __Gopal instead wrapped it in cloth and set it on his own workbench, where it stayed untouched for a week.__ When he finally began repairing it, he let me hold the thread, and I learned that some work cannot be hurried without being lost. Later the widow's grandson came to collect it, and paid in mangoes.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that the elder wanted to keep the prayer book for his own collection.
It suggests that the apprentice resented being given the simplest tasks in the workshop.
It explains why the workshop was too busy to repair the book right away.
It shows the elder's patient regard for the book, preparing the apprentice's lesson.
items.explanation: 지문 앞부분에서 Gopal은 모든 장부와 편지를 천천히 펼쳐 보는 인물로 그려지고, 화자는 서둘러 정리하려 한다. 밑줄 문장에서 Gopal은 버려질 기도서를 천에 싸서 일주일 동안 작업대에 둔다. 이후 화자는 어떤 일은 서두르면 잃는다는 교훈을 얻으므로, 밑줄 문장은 노인의 인내와 존중을 보여 주며 그 교훈을 준비한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 손자에게 돌려준 결말과 맞지 않고, B와 C는 지문 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Once, Ruoxi had believed the bus depot in Oaxaca would close before her shop did. She sold phone cards and sweet bread from a counter beside platform four, and every afternoon Valentina arrived to ask the same question: had the cousin in Puebla written back? Ruoxi always said no. __That spring, a company offered to buy the counter and the lease for more money than she had earned in a decade.__ She kept the letter folded under the cash box for a month. Valentina, still waiting for her cousin's reply, began bringing her coffee and staying through the evening rush, talking about the buses she would take once the letter came. When Ruoxi finally answered the company, she wrote only that the counter was not for sale. Outside, a driver honked twice and pulled out toward the mountains.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a chance to leave that gives the shopkeeper's choice to stay weight.
It reveals that the shopkeeper was secretly struggling to pay the depot's rising fees.
It explains why the customer visited the counter every afternoon with the same question.
It suggests that the company intended to close the depot and move the buses elsewhere.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 회사가 10년 수입보다 많은 돈으로 가게를 사겠다고 제안했다는 내용으로, 떠날 수 있는 출구를 제시한다. 이후 Ruoxi는 그 편지를 한 달간 보관하고 Valentina와 저녁을 함께 보낸 뒤 결국 팔지 않겠다고 답한다. 그러므로 이 문장은 남기로 한 결정에 무게를 더하는 기회를 소개하는 역할을 하며 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 지문에 없는 사정을 추측하고, C는 손님의 방문 이유를 잘못 연결한다.

items.passage: When I first met Tyrese, he was kneeling beside the dry fountain in a courtyard in Port of Spain, clearing leaves from a basin that had not held water in years. I had just bought the house, and I was there to plan where my mother's bed would go when she moved in from the country. Cecile, I kept telling myself, would hate the city. __Tyrese told me his own father had refused to leave his hillside until the day he could no longer climb it.__ He did not say whether that had been wise. I spent the afternoon measuring doorways and thinking less about furniture than about what my mother would lose, and what she might insist on keeping. By evening I had decided to ask her rather than tell her. Tyrese turned on the hose, and the fountain coughed rust.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why the gardener has neglected the fountain for many years.
It offers a parallel story that leads the narrator to rethink her approach.
It reveals that the gardener disapproves of the new owner's purchase of the house.
It describes the gardener's father in order to introduce a conflict over the property.
items.explanation: 화자는 어머니를 시골에서 데려올 계획만 세우며 어머니가 도시를 싫어할 것이라고 단정한다. 밑줄 문장에서 Tyrese는 언덕을 떠나지 않으려 했던 아버지 이야기를 들려주고, 이후 화자는 어머니가 잃을 것을 생각하며 통보 대신 묻기로 결심한다. 따라서 밑줄 문장은 비슷한 경험을 제시해 화자의 접근 방식을 바꾸게 하므로 B가 정답이다. A, C, D는 정원사의 태도나 재산 갈등처럼 지문에 근거가 없는 내용을 내세운다.

items.passage: Glasgow rain had pooled on the lid of the rooftop water tank where Saoirse and I used to rehearse, back when we shared a stage at a cabaret on Sauchiehall Street. I climbed up there again last winter to scatter nothing in particular, just to look. Saoirse's mother had made a lamb stew for the cast every opening night, and she never wrote the recipe down. After she died, Saoirse and I tried for years to reproduce it, arguing over thyme and barley. __Once, Ronan, the old stagehand, told us we were cooking a memory, not a stew.__ We laughed at him then. Now Saoirse lives in Cork, and when she phones, we no longer talk about ingredients. We talk about the opening nights themselves. The tank hummed under my hand, full of a cold that never quite reached the street.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that the stagehand had a better memory of the recipe than the two women did.
It reveals that the narrator and Saoirse finally abandoned cooking because of a quarrel.
It offers an insight first dismissed that anticipates the women's later shift.
It explains why the narrator has returned to the rooftop after many years away.
items.explanation: 두 사람은 오랫동안 백리향과 보리를 두고 다투며 레시피를 재현하려 했다. 밑줄 문장에서 Ronan은 그들이 스튜가 아니라 기억을 요리한다고 말하고, 당시 두 사람은 웃어넘긴다. 그러나 지금은 재료가 아니라 개막 밤 자체를 이야기하므로 그 말이 나중의 초점 변화를 예고한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 지문에 없는 사실을, D는 옥상에 온 이유를 잘못 연결한다.

items.passage: "Leave the dough, Leopoldina, it knows what to do," Wolfram said, though I had stopped being his pupil thirty years ago. We were in my bakery in Chengdu an hour before opening, and he had come, as he did every Sunday now, to watch me work. I have a habit of punching the dough twice more than it needs, a habit he spent an entire school year trying to correct in his chemistry lab, of all places. He is eighty-one. His hands tremble when he lifts a cup. Still he leans over the bowl and points, and I let him, because I know these mornings are how he goes on being a teacher. I fold the dough once, the way he wants, and leave it alone. Then the first delivery van rattles up outside, its headlights sweeping across the flour bins.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Wolfram?
options: She is irritated by his interference and wishes he would stop visiting the bakery.
She is indifferent to his advice and continues baking the way she always has.
She is fondly indulgent, letting him guide her because she values his role.
She is fearful of his judgment and anxious to prove she has become skilled.
items.explanation: 화자는 30년 전에 그의 제자가 아니게 되었지만 여전히 매주 일요일 그가 지켜보도록 허락한다. 또한 떨리는 손을 언급하면서도 그가 선생님으로 살아가는 방식이라는 것을 알기에 지시대로 반죽을 한 번만 접는다. 따라서 애정 어린 관대함을 보이는 C가 정답이다. A는 간섭에 대한 짜증으로, B는 무관심으로 잘못 읽었으며 D는 지문에 없는 두려움을 내세운다.

items.passage: Two rules held in the rented farmhouse in Galway that summer: no one read the letters alone, and no one read them after dark. Orla made the rules, and her brother kept them, mostly because he could not think of better ones. Their mother had written forty-three letters during the year she worked abroad, and the siblings opened one each evening at the kitchen table. Orla read aloud. Her brother listened and said little, because he had failed his driving test that afternoon and could not bring himself to admit it. Orla noticed his silence and did not ask; she only slowed down at the parts where their mother wrote about learning, late in life, to drive. Imani, the neighbor's girl, brought eggs at seven. Orla thanked her and set the basket on the windowsill beside the unopened envelopes.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Orla?
options: The narrator mocks her rules as rigid and pointless.
The narrator criticizes her for ignoring her brother's distress.
The narrator treats her as a distant figure whose motives are unclear.
The narrator quietly admires her tactful kindness.
items.explanation: 서술자는 Orla가 동생의 침묵을 알아차리고도 묻지 않았다고 서술한다. 또한 그녀가 어머니가 늦게 운전을 배운 대목에서 일부러 천천히 읽었다고 밝혀, 실패를 숨기는 동생을 조용히 배려하는 모습을 드러낸다. 따라서 그녀의 섬세한 친절을 조용히 존중하는 D가 정답이다. A는 규칙에 대한 조롱으로, B는 무시로 잘못 보았으며 C는 그녀의 동기가 지문에 분명히 드러난다는 점을 놓친다.

items.passage:
Hollis winds the shop clocks every Thursday,
a chore he once lost to Birdie on a bet
in the Manchester chess club, forty years back.
He still says she cheated. She still says
he moved his bishop like a man asleep.
Now she sits on the stool by the regulator
and calls out which ones run slow,
and he turns each key with the care
of someone tightening a promise.
I watch them from the counter, their quarrel
worn smooth as a pocket watch's case,
and think how a debt can turn into a vow.
Outside, the tram bells keep their own time.
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward Hollis and Birdie?
options: The speaker regards their old rivalry with fondness for the bond it has become.
The speaker views their quarrel with weary impatience because it has never been settled.
The speaker treats their ritual with detached curiosity about how antique clocks are maintained.
The speaker sees their partnership with concern that one of them is being treated unfairly.
items.explanation: 화자는 두 사람의 다툼을 '주머니시계 케이스처럼 닳아 매끄러워진' 것으로 묘사해 오랜 경쟁이 친숙한 것이 되었음을 보여 준다. 또한 내기의 빚이 맹세로 바뀌었다고 생각하며, 열쇠를 돌리는 모습을 약속을 조이는 손길에 비유한다. 따라서 그 경쟁을 애정 어린 시선으로 감상하는 A가 정답이다. B는 짜증으로, C는 시계 관리에 대한 관심으로, D는 불공정에 대한 우려로 잘못 읽었다.

items.passage: When my mother and I stood in line at the customs checkpoint in Tehran, carrying a garment bag between us like a sleeping child, we talked only about the wedding. Which caterer, which flowers, whether Felix's family would expect a second reception. We did not talk about my father, who had always been the one to handle the officers and the forms, and who had died in March. My mother answered the officer's questions too quickly, then too slowly. I noticed she had brought his old fountain pen to sign the declaration. Nicolas, my fiancé's brother, waved from beyond the glass, and she waved back with exaggerated cheer. I found it hard to watch and harder to look away. I have since come to think that her pretending was a kind of bravery I did not yet possess. The officer stamped our papers without looking up.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward her mother?
options: The narrator is embarrassed by her mother's nervousness and wishes she had traveled alone.
The narrator is tenderly respectful, seeing courage in her mother's forced cheer.
The narrator is frustrated that her mother refuses to plan the wedding in detail.
The narrator is amused by her mother's attempts to impress the officers at the checkpoint.
items.explanation: 화자는 어머니가 질문에 너무 빨리, 또 너무 느리게 답하고 남편의 만년필을 챙겨 온 모습을 세심하게 관찰한다. 또 과장된 쾌활함을 보기 힘들면서도 눈을 뗄 수 없었다고 말하고, 그 가장을 자신에게 아직 없던 용기로 해석한다. 따라서 어머니에게 애틋한 존중을 보이는 B가 정답이다. A는 당혹감과 혼자 여행하고 싶은 마음을, C와 D는 지문에 없는 좌절이나 즐거움을 내세운다.

items.passage: Static hissed from every shelf of Baraka's radio repair shop in Addis Ababa when Wanjiru brought in her late uncle's set. Baraka, a retired sailor, recognized it at once and said he had promised to fix it decades ago. Wanjiru remembered no such promise, and neither, she suspected, did he. Still, he worked on it for three evenings while she waited on a stool, and he told her stories of ports her uncle had never mentioned. On the fourth evening the radio played a song, faint but clear. Baraka seemed less pleased by the music than by the fact that she had stayed to hear it. Across the street, a vendor lowered the shutters on his stall of spices.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the passage?
options: To recount how a retired sailor repaired an old radio for a customer over several evenings
To describe the busy shops and vendors of a neighborhood in Addis Ababa at dusk
To show that kindness is always rewarded when people keep their promises to one another
To suggest that a forgotten promise serves mainly as a reason for two people to connect
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: Baraka는 Wanjiru도 자신도 기억하지 못하는 약속을 내세워 라디오를 고치며, 그동안 그녀에게 삼촌의 이야기를 들려준다. 또 그는 음악보다 그녀가 끝까지 남아 들어 주었다는 사실에 더 기뻐한다. 이 두 근거로 볼 때, 잊힌 약속은 두 사람이 이어지기 위한 구실이라는 D가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 지문 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르며, C는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: I had lent Errol eleven rupees in the spring, and he had promised to repay me by the monsoon, when he would surely be restored to the side. All that summer he sat upon the bench at our matches, and all that summer he came to me at the harbor with excuses as neatly coiled as the nets drying on the sea wall. Each excuse asked for another week. I granted them, believing a week a small thing to give a young man. Only when the rains came, and Shirin told me he had taken work hauling ice on the night boats, did I understand that every week I had lent him was a week he had spent elsewhere, and that the money had never been the larger debt. Below us, a trawler nosed into its berth, its deck silver with pomfret and its crew shouting for the scales.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To depict the narrator's dawning sense that the time he granted Errol cost more than the money
To recount how Errol sat on the bench all summer while repeatedly delaying repayment of a small loan
To describe the working life of the harbor, where nets, ice boats, and trawlers shape each day
To suggest that generosity toward others is usually repaid with disappointment and regret
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 Errol의 핑계마다 '한 주'를 더 내주며 그것을 작은 일로 여긴다. 뒷부분에서 Errol이 다른 일을 하고 있었음을 알게 된 화자는 빌려준 시간이 돈보다 더 큰 빚이었음을 깨닫는다. 따라서 두 부분을 연결한 A가 서술 목적이다. B는 일화만 요약했고, C는 항구 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Ruwan had cooked for the summer camp in Karachi for nineteen years, and on my first visit as her son's wife, I watched the camp director praise her dal before two hundred children. Everyone applauded. Afterward, in the steam behind the serving counter, she counted the onions she had bought with her own money and wrote the sum in a small notebook no one had ever asked to see. The next week the director thanked me, too, for the rotis I had rolled, and Danish beamed as though I had won a prize. I found Ruwan's notebook on the shelf that evening; my name had already been added beneath hers, with an empty column waiting. Outside, the boys were dragging benches across the courtyard for the evening's talent show, arguing over who would sit nearest the fan.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The narrator recalls helping Ruwan cook for the children during her first visit to the camp.
The praise both women receive at the camp conceals labor and expense that go unrewarded.
The camp is portrayed as a lively place where children gather for meals and shows.
Families grow closer when they share the work of feeding others in their community.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Ruwan은 박수를 받지만 자기 돈으로 산 양파 값을 아무도 보지 않는 공책에 적는다. 뒷부분에서 화자도 감사 인사를 받은 뒤 그 공책에 자기 이름과 빈 칸이 추가된 것을 발견한다. 두 장면을 이으면 칭찬 뒤에 보상받지 못하는 노동이 숨어 있다는 B가 요지다. A는 일화 요약, C는 소재만 쓴 다른 목적, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Years later, Despina would remember that the floodlights had not yet come on when she found the envelope. It had slipped from Kostas's music case onto the grass beside the soccer field, where he liked to walk his students after lessons, and it was addressed not to her but to the conservatory in Vienna. Through the thin paper she could read her own name beside the words regrettably not ready. She thought of the scale he had made her repeat forty times that afternoon, and of how he had said, almost gently, that Vienna would ask for more. She tucked the envelope back into the case without a word and asked him for one more hour of lessons each week. On the far side of the field, boys were still kicking a ball toward a goal they could barely see.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Despina most likely ask Kostas for more lessons?
options: She is ashamed of having read a letter that was never meant for her eyes.
She wants Kostas to rewrite his letter and praise her to the conservatory.
She has been told by the conservatory that she must repeat her scales.
She wants to meet the standard Kostas thinks the conservatory will demand.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 단서를 두 문장 이상 연결해야 하며 오답 중 하나는 결과를 동기로 착각하는 전형적 오독이다
items.explanation: Despina는 편지에서 자신이 아직 준비되지 않았다는 평가를 읽는다. 이어 그녀는 Kostas가 빈은 더 많은 것을 요구할 것이라고 말한 일을 떠올린다. 두 단서를 연결하면 그 기준에 도달하려고 수업을 늘린다는 D가 동기다. A는 다른 감정, B는 행동의 결과를 동기로 착각한 것, C는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: Salt stung the cut on Renata's knuckle as she lowered herself into the pool carved from the black rock. Mingyu was already there, floating on his back the way he had when her father still came to Jeju each summer. He was selling his dive shop and moving to Busan for good, he had told her, and he had a box of her father's things he did not know what to do with. Inside, she had found a logbook filled with dives the two men had made together, each entry signed by both. Now she swam to him and asked, before she could lose her nerve, whether he would teach her the route from the last page. He was quiet, then nodded toward the reef. Gulls wheeled over the breakwater, quarreling over a fish one of them had dropped.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Renata most likely ask Mingyu to teach her the route?
options: She wants to share part of her father's life with Mingyu before he leaves.
She is angry that Mingyu kept her father's belongings for so many years.
She hopes the lesson will persuade Mingyu to keep his dive shop open.
She was asked by her father to complete the dives in his old logbook.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 단서를 두 문장 이상 연결해야 하며 오답 중 하나는 결과를 동기로 착각하는 전형적 오독이다
items.explanation: Mingyu가 가게를 팔고 영영 떠난다는 사실과, 로그북에 두 사람이 함께한 잠수가 서명과 함께 기록되어 있다는 사실이 단서다. 두 문장을 이으면 Renata는 그가 떠나기 전에 아버지의 삶 일부를 그와 함께 나누고 싶어 한다는 A가 동기다. B는 지문에 없는 다른 감정, C는 행동의 결과를 동기로 착각한 것, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: Once, in a laundromat near the Beirut harbor, I folded sheets beside a woman who had ridden my father's ferry that morning. Fiorella, she said her name was, and she was mending a sail for the yacht club, a job she had been hired for alone. I knew something of sails; my father's had torn every spring, and I, Tamika, had patched them since I was nine. When she struggled with the seam, I showed her the double stitch, and we finished the work together while the machines rattled. She thanked me warmly and said the club would be delighted with her. Weeks earlier, I had watched my father accept praise for patches I had sewn. So I wrote my initials, small, in the corner of the canvas. The attendant came by then, mopping soap from the floor.
items.question: Based on the text, why does the narrator most likely write her initials on the canvas?
options: She is proud of the double stitch and wants Fiorella to remember how to sew it.
She wants a lasting mark of her share in work that others are likely to claim.
She hopes the yacht club will notice her initials and hire her for future repairs.
She was told by her father that every sail she patched should carry her name.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 단서를 두 문장 이상 연결해야 하며 오답 중 하나는 결과를 동기로 착각하는 전형적 오독이다
items.explanation: Fiorella는 함께 끝낸 작업을 두고 클럽이 '자신에게' 만족할 것이라고 말한다. 화자는 몇 주 전 아버지가 자신이 꿰맨 천에 대한 칭찬을 받던 일도 떠올린다. 두 단서를 이으면 남이 가져갈 공로에 자기 몫을 남기려는 B가 동기다. A는 다른 감정, C는 행동의 결과를 동기로 착각한 것, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: Bay rum and scorched hair hung in the air as Itzel snapped a cape around my father's neck. Bogdan had lived in Havana for thirty years and still refused to speak Spanish in her shop, so I was, as always, his translator. Short on the sides, he told me in Russian, not too much on top. I told Itzel to take it all off. She raised her scissors and grinned at me in the mirror, and I grinned back, because he had been telling me for weeks that I was too stubborn to cut my own hair. Only when the first gray lock slid down the cape did I notice his hands tightening on the armrests. Itzel hummed along with the radio, a bolero about a sailor and a faraway port.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Uneasy and apprehensive, focused on the father's tightening grip on the chair
Uneasy with brief flashes of humor, dwelling mostly on the father's distress
Playfully mischievous, though shadowed by a growing hint of unease
Nostalgic and wistful, recalling the narrator's childhood visits to the shop
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 정서의 비중을 판단해야 하며, 오답은 정반대가 아니라 비중이 틀린 어조다
items.explanation: 화자는 아버지의 말을 일부러 바꿔 통역하고 이발사와 거울 속에서 서로 웃으며 장난을 즐긴다. 그러나 첫 머리카락이 떨어질 때 아버지의 손이 팔걸이를 움켜쥐는 것을 보고 불안이 스민다. 장난기가 더 두드러지고 불안이 뒤따르므로 C가 맞다. A는 덜 두드러진 정서만, B는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었고, D는 지문에 단서가 약하다.

items.passage: We have been waiting since noon, you and your grandfather, on the orange chairs outside the scan room. To pass the time, Haruto takes a photograph from his wallet: a boy on a snowbank, holding a fish nearly as long as himself. You try the word for proud and get it wrong, and he laughs so loudly that the nurse at the desk looks up. He corrects you, slowly, tapping each syllable on your wrist, Mio, the way he once tapped rhythms for you on the kitchen table. Twice he glances at the door when it opens, and twice he goes back to the photograph as if it were a lesson he must finish. You say the word again, correctly this time. Outside the window, a snowplow scrapes along the empty lot, its yellow light turning in the dusk.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Anxious and fearful, centered on the results of the grandfather's scan
Tense and apprehensive, softened by brief moments of shared laughter
Mournful and elegiac, lamenting a childhood that can never return
Affectionate and gently humorous, with an undercurrent of worry
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 정서의 비중을 판단해야 하며, 오답은 정반대가 아니라 비중이 틀린 어조다
items.explanation: 할아버지는 손녀의 틀린 발음에 크게 웃고 음절을 손목에 두드려 주며 다정하게 가르친다. 동시에 문이 열릴 때마다 시선을 돌리는 모습에서 검사 결과에 대한 걱정이 은근히 드러난다. 다정함이 두드러지고 걱정이 밑에 깔려 있으므로 D가 맞다. A는 덜 두드러진 정서만, B는 비중을 뒤집었고, C는 단서가 약한 어조다.

items.passage: “They have locked the reading room for the inspector,” the woman beside me said, and that was how I, Anushka, met Zofia. We sat together on the bench in the corridor of the Tbilisi library, two strangers with nowhere to be for an hour. She was reading the same pamphlet I was, a tribute to the professor whose portrait hung above us. When I mentioned that my aunt had typed his famous lectures, Zofia closed the pamphlet and said quietly that her mother had written them. For a moment neither of us spoke. Then she slid half of her bread across the bench to me, and I offered her my aunt's address. A clerk passed with a cart of ledgers, one wheel squeaking at every tile.
items.question: Which choice best describes the relationship between Anushka and Zofia that develops in the text?
options: Two strangers drawn into a quiet alliance by a shared discovery about the professor
A stranger who pities a woman whose mother was never credited for her lectures
Rivals competing to prove whose relative truly earned the professor's reputation
A scholar and an admirer united by their deep respect for a famous professor
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 문장의 단서를 연결해야 하고 오답은 한쪽 감정만 반영한다
items.explanation: Anushka의 이모가 강의를 타이핑했고 Zofia의 어머니가 그 강의를 썼다는 사실이 대화로 드러난다. 이어 Zofia가 빵을 나누고 Anushka가 주소를 건네는 행동에서 두 사람이 비밀을 공유한 연대 관계가 됨을 알 수 있다. 따라서 A가 맞다. B는 한쪽 감정만, C는 방향이 반대인 관계, D는 일반적 통념에서 고른 관계다.

items.passage: Greta did not want to sell. She pushed her mother's chair along the promenade each afternoon, past the pier where the steamers unloaded, and each afternoon her mother raised the matter of the house in Blankenese. The roof leaks, the old woman said, and you cannot nurse me and mend slates at once. Greta tucked the blanket tighter around her mother's knees and pointed out a ship flying a Norwegian flag. Later, when her mother asked whether the agent had written again, Greta answered that the letter must have gone astray, though it lay folded in her coat pocket. Her mother reached up and patted the hand on the chair. Along the railing, a vendor was selling smoked eel wrapped in newspaper.
items.question: Which choice best describes the relationship between Greta and her mother?
options: A frustrated daughter grown tired of her mother's constant talk about the house
A protective daughter deflecting a mother who gently accepts her evasions
A daughter pressing her reluctant mother to agree to sell the family house
A grateful mother and daughter made inseparable by their shared hardships
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 문장의 단서를 연결해야 하고 오답은 한쪽 감정만 반영한다
items.explanation: Greta는 어머니가 집 문제를 꺼낼 때마다 담요를 여며 주며 화제를 돌리고, 중개인의 편지도 숨긴다. 어머니는 그 거짓을 짐작하는 듯 딸의 손을 토닥인다. 두 행동을 이으면 B가 관계를 가장 잘 설명한다. A는 한쪽 감정만, C는 방향이 반대인 관계, D는 일반적 통념에서 고른 관계다.

items.passage: Years ago, when I was foreman of the crew that laid the tiles at the new metro station in Lima, I wrote an apology to Linh, the youngest of my workers, whom I had blamed before everyone for a cracked step that was not his doing. I, Ofelia, carried the letter in my vest for a week. Each evening I waited on the platform where he caught his train, and each evening a car pulled in, its doors opened, and I let it go. Linh would board, nod to me through the glass, and be carried off toward the hills. On the seventh evening the doors opened again and closed again, and I watched the red lamp of the last car dwindle into the tunnel. The paper had gone soft at the folds by then. Above the platform, pigeons settled along the iron beams, shaking dust from their feathers.
items.question: In the text, the trains that the narrator lets depart most likely represent
options: the speed with which the young hire advances beyond his foreman's crew.
the new station's progress, which the narrator's crew helped bring about.
the narrator's repeated chances to apologize, each allowed to pass.
the distance between the city center and the hills where Linh lives.
items.explanation: 화자는 사과 편지를 품고 매일 저녁 승강장에서 기다리지만 열차가 문을 열 때마다 그대로 보낸다. 이 장면이 일주일 동안 반복되고 마지막 열차가 터널로 사라지므로, 열차는 매번 놓쳐 버린 사과의 기회를 상징한다. 따라서 C가 맞다. A, B, D는 열차와 역의 소재를 쓰지만 사과와의 연결을 놓친다.

## 문항
### lit40-medium-05-031 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 underlined_portion_function
[지문]
I had been Gopal's apprentice in the bookbinding workshop in Dhaka for only a year when we were hired to empty a widow's house. My name is Efua, and I was restless then; I wanted to sort everything into piles and be done by noon. Gopal moved slowly, opening each ledger and letter as if it might speak. By evening only one item remained: a ragged prayer book with its spine split in three places. I offered to throw it on the cart. __Gopal instead wrapped it in cloth and set it on his own workbench, where it stayed untouched for a week.__ When he finally began repairing it, he let me hold the thread, and I learned that some work cannot be hurried without being lost. Later the widow's grandson came to collect it, and paid in mangoes.

[질문] Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
A) It shows that the elder wanted to keep the prayer book for his own collection.
B) It suggests that the apprentice resented being given the simplest tasks in the workshop.
C) It explains why the workshop was too busy to repair the book right away.
D) It shows the elder's patient regard for the book, preparing the apprentice's lesson.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
지문 앞부분에서 Gopal은 모든 장부와 편지를 천천히 펼쳐 보는 인물로 그려지고, 화자는 서둘러 정리하려 한다. 밑줄 문장에서 Gopal은 버려질 기도서를 천에 싸서 일주일 동안 작업대에 둔다. 이후 화자는 어떤 일은 서두르면 잃는다는 교훈을 얻으므로, 밑줄 문장은 노인의 인내와 존중을 보여 주며 그 교훈을 준비한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 손자에게 돌려준 결말과 맞지 않고, B와 C는 지문 근거가 없다.
### lit40-medium-05-032 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 underlined_portion_function
[지문]
Once, Ruoxi had believed the bus depot in Oaxaca would close before her shop did. She sold phone cards and sweet bread from a counter beside platform four, and every afternoon Valentina arrived to ask the same question: had the cousin in Puebla written back? Ruoxi always said no. __That spring, a company offered to buy the counter and the lease for more money than she had earned in a decade.__ She kept the letter folded under the cash box for a month. Valentina, still waiting for her cousin's reply, began bringing her coffee and staying through the evening rush, talking about the buses she would take once the letter came. When Ruoxi finally answered the company, she wrote only that the counter was not for sale. Outside, a driver honked twice and pulled out toward the mountains.

[질문] Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
A) It introduces a chance to leave that gives the shopkeeper's choice to stay weight.
B) It reveals that the shopkeeper was secretly struggling to pay the depot's rising fees.
C) It explains why the customer visited the counter every afternoon with the same question.
D) It suggests that the company intended to close the depot and move the buses elsewhere.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
밑줄 문장은 회사가 10년 수입보다 많은 돈으로 가게를 사겠다고 제안했다는 내용으로, 떠날 수 있는 출구를 제시한다. 이후 Ruoxi는 그 편지를 한 달간 보관하고 Valentina와 저녁을 함께 보낸 뒤 결국 팔지 않겠다고 답한다. 그러므로 이 문장은 남기로 한 결정에 무게를 더하는 기회를 소개하는 역할을 하며 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 지문에 없는 사정을 추측하고, C는 손님의 방문 이유를 잘못 연결한다.
### lit40-medium-05-033 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 underlined_portion_function
[지문]
When I first met Tyrese, he was kneeling beside the dry fountain in a courtyard in Port of Spain, clearing leaves from a basin that had not held water in years. I had just bought the house, and I was there to plan where my mother's bed would go when she moved in from the country. Cecile, I kept telling myself, would hate the city. __Tyrese told me his own father had refused to leave his hillside until the day he could no longer climb it.__ He did not say whether that had been wise. I spent the afternoon measuring doorways and thinking less about furniture than about what my mother would lose, and what she might insist on keeping. By evening I had decided to ask her rather than tell her. Tyrese turned on the hose, and the fountain coughed rust.

[질문] Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
A) It explains why the gardener has neglected the fountain for many years.
B) It offers a parallel story that leads the narrator to rethink her approach.
C) It reveals that the gardener disapproves of the new owner's purchase of the house.
D) It describes the gardener's father in order to introduce a conflict over the property.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
화자는 어머니를 시골에서 데려올 계획만 세우며 어머니가 도시를 싫어할 것이라고 단정한다. 밑줄 문장에서 Tyrese는 언덕을 떠나지 않으려 했던 아버지 이야기를 들려주고, 이후 화자는 어머니가 잃을 것을 생각하며 통보 대신 묻기로 결심한다. 따라서 밑줄 문장은 비슷한 경험을 제시해 화자의 접근 방식을 바꾸게 하므로 B가 정답이다. A, C, D는 정원사의 태도나 재산 갈등처럼 지문에 근거가 없는 내용을 내세운다.
### lit40-medium-05-034 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 underlined_portion_function
[지문]
Glasgow rain had pooled on the lid of the rooftop water tank where Saoirse and I used to rehearse, back when we shared a stage at a cabaret on Sauchiehall Street. I climbed up there again last winter to scatter nothing in particular, just to look. Saoirse's mother had made a lamb stew for the cast every opening night, and she never wrote the recipe down. After she died, Saoirse and I tried for years to reproduce it, arguing over thyme and barley. __Once, Ronan, the old stagehand, told us we were cooking a memory, not a stew.__ We laughed at him then. Now Saoirse lives in Cork, and when she phones, we no longer talk about ingredients. We talk about the opening nights themselves. The tank hummed under my hand, full of a cold that never quite reached the street.

[질문] Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
A) It shows that the stagehand had a better memory of the recipe than the two women did.
B) It reveals that the narrator and Saoirse finally abandoned cooking because of a quarrel.
C) It offers an insight first dismissed that anticipates the women's later shift.
D) It explains why the narrator has returned to the rooftop after many years away.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
두 사람은 오랫동안 백리향과 보리를 두고 다투며 레시피를 재현하려 했다. 밑줄 문장에서 Ronan은 그들이 스튜가 아니라 기억을 요리한다고 말하고, 당시 두 사람은 웃어넘긴다. 그러나 지금은 재료가 아니라 개막 밤 자체를 이야기하므로 그 말이 나중의 초점 변화를 예고한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 지문에 없는 사실을, D는 옥상에 온 이유를 잘못 연결한다.
### lit40-medium-05-035 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
"Leave the dough, Leopoldina, it knows what to do," Wolfram said, though I had stopped being his pupil thirty years ago. We were in my bakery in Chengdu an hour before opening, and he had come, as he did every Sunday now, to watch me work. I have a habit of punching the dough twice more than it needs, a habit he spent an entire school year trying to correct in his chemistry lab, of all places. He is eighty-one. His hands tremble when he lifts a cup. Still he leans over the bowl and points, and I let him, because I know these mornings are how he goes on being a teacher. I fold the dough once, the way he wants, and leave it alone. Then the first delivery van rattles up outside, its headlights sweeping across the flour bins.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Wolfram?
A) She is irritated by his interference and wishes he would stop visiting the bakery.
B) She is indifferent to his advice and continues baking the way she always has.
C) She is fondly indulgent, letting him guide her because she values his role.
D) She is fearful of his judgment and anxious to prove she has become skilled.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
화자는 30년 전에 그의 제자가 아니게 되었지만 여전히 매주 일요일 그가 지켜보도록 허락한다. 또한 떨리는 손을 언급하면서도 그가 선생님으로 살아가는 방식이라는 것을 알기에 지시대로 반죽을 한 번만 접는다. 따라서 애정 어린 관대함을 보이는 C가 정답이다. A는 간섭에 대한 짜증으로, B는 무관심으로 잘못 읽었으며 D는 지문에 없는 두려움을 내세운다.
### lit40-medium-05-036 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
Two rules held in the rented farmhouse in Galway that summer: no one read the letters alone, and no one read them after dark. Orla made the rules, and her brother kept them, mostly because he could not think of better ones. Their mother had written forty-three letters during the year she worked abroad, and the siblings opened one each evening at the kitchen table. Orla read aloud. Her brother listened and said little, because he had failed his driving test that afternoon and could not bring himself to admit it. Orla noticed his silence and did not ask; she only slowed down at the parts where their mother wrote about learning, late in life, to drive. Imani, the neighbor's girl, brought eggs at seven. Orla thanked her and set the basket on the windowsill beside the unopened envelopes.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Orla?
A) The narrator mocks her rules as rigid and pointless.
B) The narrator criticizes her for ignoring her brother's distress.
C) The narrator treats her as a distant figure whose motives are unclear.
D) The narrator quietly admires her tactful kindness.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
서술자는 Orla가 동생의 침묵을 알아차리고도 묻지 않았다고 서술한다. 또한 그녀가 어머니가 늦게 운전을 배운 대목에서 일부러 천천히 읽었다고 밝혀, 실패를 숨기는 동생을 조용히 배려하는 모습을 드러낸다. 따라서 그녀의 섬세한 친절을 조용히 존중하는 D가 정답이다. A는 규칙에 대한 조롱으로, B는 무시로 잘못 보았으며 C는 그녀의 동기가 지문에 분명히 드러난다는 점을 놓친다.
### lit40-medium-05-037 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
Hollis winds the shop clocks every Thursday,
a chore he once lost to Birdie on a bet
in the Manchester chess club, forty years back.
He still says she cheated. She still says
he moved his bishop like a man asleep.
Now she sits on the stool by the regulator
and calls out which ones run slow,
and he turns each key with the care
of someone tightening a promise.
I watch them from the counter, their quarrel
worn smooth as a pocket watch's case,
and think how a debt can turn into a vow.
Outside, the tram bells keep their own time.

[질문] Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward Hollis and Birdie?
A) The speaker regards their old rivalry with fondness for the bond it has become.
B) The speaker views their quarrel with weary impatience because it has never been settled.
C) The speaker treats their ritual with detached curiosity about how antique clocks are maintained.
D) The speaker sees their partnership with concern that one of them is being treated unfairly.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
화자는 두 사람의 다툼을 '주머니시계 케이스처럼 닳아 매끄러워진' 것으로 묘사해 오랜 경쟁이 친숙한 것이 되었음을 보여 준다. 또한 내기의 빚이 맹세로 바뀌었다고 생각하며, 열쇠를 돌리는 모습을 약속을 조이는 손길에 비유한다. 따라서 그 경쟁을 애정 어린 시선으로 감상하는 A가 정답이다. B는 짜증으로, C는 시계 관리에 대한 관심으로, D는 불공정에 대한 우려로 잘못 읽었다.
### lit40-medium-05-038 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
When my mother and I stood in line at the customs checkpoint in Tehran, carrying a garment bag between us like a sleeping child, we talked only about the wedding. Which caterer, which flowers, whether Felix's family would expect a second reception. We did not talk about my father, who had always been the one to handle the officers and the forms, and who had died in March. My mother answered the officer's questions too quickly, then too slowly. I noticed she had brought his old fountain pen to sign the declaration. Nicolas, my fiancé's brother, waved from beyond the glass, and she waved back with exaggerated cheer. I found it hard to watch and harder to look away. I have since come to think that her pretending was a kind of bravery I did not yet possess. The officer stamped our papers without looking up.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward her mother?
A) The narrator is embarrassed by her mother's nervousness and wishes she had traveled alone.
B) The narrator is tenderly respectful, seeing courage in her mother's forced cheer.
C) The narrator is frustrated that her mother refuses to plan the wedding in detail.
D) The narrator is amused by her mother's attempts to impress the officers at the checkpoint.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
화자는 어머니가 질문에 너무 빨리, 또 너무 느리게 답하고 남편의 만년필을 챙겨 온 모습을 세심하게 관찰한다. 또 과장된 쾌활함을 보기 힘들면서도 눈을 뗄 수 없었다고 말하고, 그 가장을 자신에게 아직 없던 용기로 해석한다. 따라서 어머니에게 애틋한 존중을 보이는 B가 정답이다. A는 당혹감과 혼자 여행하고 싶은 마음을, C와 D는 지문에 없는 좌절이나 즐거움을 내세운다.
### lit40-medium-05-040 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
Static hissed from every shelf of Baraka's radio repair shop in Addis Ababa when Wanjiru brought in her late uncle's set. Baraka, a retired sailor, recognized it at once and said he had promised to fix it decades ago. Wanjiru remembered no such promise, and neither, she suspected, did he. Still, he worked on it for three evenings while she waited on a stool, and he told her stories of ports her uncle had never mentioned. On the fourth evening the radio played a song, faint but clear. Baraka seemed less pleased by the music than by the fact that she had stayed to hear it. Across the street, a vendor lowered the shutters on his stall of spices.

[질문] Which choice best states the main purpose of the passage?
A) To recount how a retired sailor repaired an old radio for a customer over several evenings
B) To describe the busy shops and vendors of a neighborhood in Addis Ababa at dusk
C) To show that kindness is always rewarded when people keep their promises to one another
D) To suggest that a forgotten promise serves mainly as a reason for two people to connect

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
Baraka는 Wanjiru도 자신도 기억하지 못하는 약속을 내세워 라디오를 고치며, 그동안 그녀에게 삼촌의 이야기를 들려준다. 또 그는 음악보다 그녀가 끝까지 남아 들어 주었다는 사실에 더 기뻐한다. 이 두 근거로 볼 때, 잊힌 약속은 두 사람이 이어지기 위한 구실이라는 D가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 지문 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르며, C는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.
### lit40-medium-05-041 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
I had lent Errol eleven rupees in the spring, and he had promised to repay me by the monsoon, when he would surely be restored to the side. All that summer he sat upon the bench at our matches, and all that summer he came to me at the harbor with excuses as neatly coiled as the nets drying on the sea wall. Each excuse asked for another week. I granted them, believing a week a small thing to give a young man. Only when the rains came, and Shirin told me he had taken work hauling ice on the night boats, did I understand that every week I had lent him was a week he had spent elsewhere, and that the money had never been the larger debt. Below us, a trawler nosed into its berth, its deck silver with pomfret and its crew shouting for the scales.

[질문] Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
A) To depict the narrator's dawning sense that the time he granted Errol cost more than the money
B) To recount how Errol sat on the bench all summer while repeatedly delaying repayment of a small loan
C) To describe the working life of the harbor, where nets, ice boats, and trawlers shape each day
D) To suggest that generosity toward others is usually repaid with disappointment and regret

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
앞부분에서 화자는 Errol의 핑계마다 '한 주'를 더 내주며 그것을 작은 일로 여긴다. 뒷부분에서 Errol이 다른 일을 하고 있었음을 알게 된 화자는 빌려준 시간이 돈보다 더 큰 빚이었음을 깨닫는다. 따라서 두 부분을 연결한 A가 서술 목적이다. B는 일화만 요약했고, C는 항구 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.
### lit40-medium-05-042 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
Ruwan had cooked for the summer camp in Karachi for nineteen years, and on my first visit as her son's wife, I watched the camp director praise her dal before two hundred children. Everyone applauded. Afterward, in the steam behind the serving counter, she counted the onions she had bought with her own money and wrote the sum in a small notebook no one had ever asked to see. The next week the director thanked me, too, for the rotis I had rolled, and Danish beamed as though I had won a prize. I found Ruwan's notebook on the shelf that evening; my name had already been added beneath hers, with an empty column waiting. Outside, the boys were dragging benches across the courtyard for the evening's talent show, arguing over who would sit nearest the fan.

[질문] Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) The narrator recalls helping Ruwan cook for the children during her first visit to the camp.
B) The praise both women receive at the camp conceals labor and expense that go unrewarded.
C) The camp is portrayed as a lively place where children gather for meals and shows.
D) Families grow closer when they share the work of feeding others in their community.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
앞부분에서 Ruwan은 박수를 받지만 자기 돈으로 산 양파 값을 아무도 보지 않는 공책에 적는다. 뒷부분에서 화자도 감사 인사를 받은 뒤 그 공책에 자기 이름과 빈 칸이 추가된 것을 발견한다. 두 장면을 이으면 칭찬 뒤에 보상받지 못하는 노동이 숨어 있다는 B가 요지다. A는 일화 요약, C는 소재만 쓴 다른 목적, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.
### lit40-medium-05-044 — skill inferences · 유형 character_motivation
[지문]
Years later, Despina would remember that the floodlights had not yet come on when she found the envelope. It had slipped from Kostas's music case onto the grass beside the soccer field, where he liked to walk his students after lessons, and it was addressed not to her but to the conservatory in Vienna. Through the thin paper she could read her own name beside the words regrettably not ready. She thought of the scale he had made her repeat forty times that afternoon, and of how he had said, almost gently, that Vienna would ask for more. She tucked the envelope back into the case without a word and asked him for one more hour of lessons each week. On the far side of the field, boys were still kicking a ball toward a goal they could barely see.

[질문] Based on the text, why does Despina most likely ask Kostas for more lessons?
A) She is ashamed of having read a letter that was never meant for her eyes.
B) She wants Kostas to rewrite his letter and praise her to the conservatory.
C) She has been told by the conservatory that she must repeat her scales.
D) She wants to meet the standard Kostas thinks the conservatory will demand.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
Despina는 편지에서 자신이 아직 준비되지 않았다는 평가를 읽는다. 이어 그녀는 Kostas가 빈은 더 많은 것을 요구할 것이라고 말한 일을 떠올린다. 두 단서를 연결하면 그 기준에 도달하려고 수업을 늘린다는 D가 동기다. A는 다른 감정, B는 행동의 결과를 동기로 착각한 것, C는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.
### lit40-medium-05-045 — skill inferences · 유형 character_motivation
[지문]
Salt stung the cut on Renata's knuckle as she lowered herself into the pool carved from the black rock. Mingyu was already there, floating on his back the way he had when her father still came to Jeju each summer. Inside, she had found a logbook filled with dives the two men had made together, each entry signed by both. Now she swam to him and asked, before she could lose her nerve, whether he would teach her the route from the last page. He was quiet, then nodded toward the reef. Gulls wheeled over the breakwater, quarreling over a fish one of them had dropped.

[질문] Based on the text, why does Renata most likely ask Mingyu to teach her the route?
A) She wants to share part of her father's life with Mingyu before he leaves.
B) She is angry that Mingyu kept her father's belongings for so many years.

### lit40-medium-05-046 — skill inferences · 유형 character_motivation
[지문]
Once, in a laundromat near the Beirut harbor, I folded sheets beside a woman who had ridden my father's ferry that morning. I knew something of sails; my father's had torn every spring, and I, Tamika, had patched them since I was nine. When she struggled with the seam, I showed her the double stitch, and we finished the work together while the machines rattled. She thanked me warmly and said the club would be delighted with her. [질문] Based on the text, why does the narrator most likely write her initials on the canvas?
A) She is proud of the double stitch and wants Fiorella to remember how to sew it.
B) She wants a lasting mark of her share in work that others are likely to claim.
C) She hopes the yacht club will notice her initials and hire her for future repairs.
D) She was told by her father that every sail she patched should carry her name.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
Fiorella는 함께 끝낸 작업을 두고 클럽이 '자신에게' 만족할 것이라고 말한다. 화자는 몇 주 전 아버지가 자신이 꿰맨 천에 대한 칭찬을 받던 일도 떠올린다. 두 단서를 이으면 남이 가져갈 공로에 자기 몫을 남기려는 B가 동기다. A는 다른 감정, C는 행동의 결과를 동기로 착각한 것, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.
### lit40-medium-05-047 — skill inferences · 유형 tone_or_mood
[지문]
Bay rum and scorched hair hung in the air as Itzel snapped a cape around my father's neck. Bogdan had lived in Havana for thirty years and still refused to speak Spanish in her shop, so I was, as always, his translator. Short on the sides, he told me in Russian, not too much on top. I told Itzel to take it all off. She raised her scissors and grinned at me in the mirror, and I grinned back, because he had been telling me for weeks that I was too stubborn to cut my own hair. A) Uneasy and apprehensive, focused on the father's tightening grip on the chair

[지문]

### lit40-medium-05-049 — skill inferences · 유형 relationship_between_characters

### lit40-medium-05-051 — skill inferences · 유형 symbolism
[지문]

A) the speed with which the young hire advances beyond his foreman's crew.
B) the new station's progress, which the narrator's crew helped bring about.

D) the distance between the city center and the hills where Linh lives.
